text:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT ALERT: High latency observed on hosted /v1/generate endpoints. PagerDuty triggered for on-call. Impact: increased p50/p95 across multiple regions, some customers seeing timeouts. Auto-remediation: none. Paging Alice K.

Alice K: I'm on call. seeing p50 jump from ~120ms -> ~220ms and p95 from ~420ms -> ~1.2s for the last 18m. CPU on model hosts seems normal but tail is bad. Starting triage. @eng-sre @eng-runtime please ping in.

Maya R: Posting graphs — overall latency spike starts ~16:02 UTC, aligns with a rolling infra change window we had this morning (16:00-16:10). Link: https://graphs.internal/redwood/latency?range=30m (shared). p50 and p95 heatmap attached.

Ben T: Checking traces now. Quick note: traces show long blocking on `futex_wait` and long kernel syscalls inside the request-serving threads. Not seeing obvious GRPC retries.

Priya S: perf counters from one affected host (snip):
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T16:07:34Z
cpu0  cpu1  cpu2  cpu3
%idle  12.3  10.9  9.8  11.0
%iowait 4.6  5.2  5.1  4.9
softirq  35k/s -> 120k/s
context-switches elevated
```
This suggests kernel-side scheduling/softirq pressure.

Jonathan L: Any recent kernel upgrades on those nodes? We rolled a security kernel bump to 5.15.0-1024 across the cluster earlier today in the 16:00 window (scheduled). Can someone list apt/upgrade history on one affected node?

Ben T: Ran `ssh node-12 && cat /var/log/apt/history.log | tail -n 40` -> shows: `linux-image-5.15.0-1024 installed at 16:03:12`. Also `dmesg` shows a bunch of `futex` stalls: 
```
[  960.123456] WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 2345 at kernel/futex.c:xyz futex_wait+0xabc/0xdef
[  960.123457] INFO: Backtrace:
[  960.123458] task my-service  ppid:1  stack: 0xffff...
```

Alice K: Hypotheses so far: (1) kernel regression from the 5.15.0-1024 -> increased futex/syscall latency under our workload, (2) new runtime change triggered additional contention (less likely, no runtime roll today), (3) GPU driver / NVMe driver edge case. We need quick live mitigation to reduce customer impact.

Dave P: For immediate mitigation: 1) revert traffic away from affected nodes (drain NodeGroup-a), 2) temporarily move some requests to Dedicated cluster for heavy tails, 3) add a short-term p95 alert throttle to protect UI-facing customers. Ops can we drain a node and boot it with previous kernel 5.15.0-1022 as a canary?

Ben T: Draining node-12 now: `kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> successful, pods scheduled elsewhere. Booting with old kernel via cloud-init snapshot now (in progress).

Leah C (support): Customer-impact update: ~8 paid customers reported slow responses, two submitted support tickets. No data loss. I'm messaging affected customers with an initial incident notification and ETA for mitigation.

Priya S: Collected `perf top` on an affected host before drain: top symbols: `futex_wait`, `do_syscall_64`, `__schedule`, high contention in user-threads waiting on mutexes. NVMe I/O latency is normal.

Maya R: After draining the first canary node and routing away traffic, we see partial recovery in that node's pods when rescheduled on other nodes. Cluster-wide p95 drops by ~30% but still above baseline. Still seeing spikes in region-b.

Jonathan L: Can we correlate host kernel versions vs. p95 by node? I ran `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and crossref with `/var/log/apt/history.log` from nodes. Nodes with 5.15.0-1024 match 90% of the high-tail hosts. That's pretty suggestive.

Alice K: Handing off to Ben T for the hands-on rollback and deeper RCA. I'm available on the watch but will switch to support coordination. Ben, take over.

Ben T: I'll continue. Plan: 1) Roll one node back to 5.15.0-1022 and keep it in service as a control for 10m, 2) If p95 improves on traffic routed to rollback nodes, escalate to infra to stop the kernel rollout and coordinate a cluster-wide rollback, 3) Collect perf and strace traces for deeper root cause.

Ben T: After rollback of node-12 -> 5.15.0-1022 and rejoin, routing 20% of traffic via tags to node-12. Observed p95 on node-12-backed requests drop to ~480ms vs cluster 920-1200ms. Initial result: rollback improves tail.

Priya S: strace snippet from an effected process (pre-rollback):
```
futex(0x7f8c1a2b4c, FUTEX_WAIT, 2, NULL) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
sched_yield() = 0
futex(0x7f8c1a2b4c, FUTEX_WAIT, 2, NULL) = -1 EAGAIN
```
Multiple threads blocked on futex for 500-1000ms intervals.

Dave P: Given canary rollback improvement, aborting automated kernel roll for remaining nodes. Ops: hold the rollout, create a block in the deployment pipeline and notify kernel vendor.

Maya R: System metrics after canary rollback (3m after): overall p95 down ~55% relative to peak, error rates stable, CPU utilization same. Attaching mini timeline: 16:00 kernel roll started -> 16:07 p95 spike -> 16:12 canary drain -> 16:25 canary rollback -> 16:33 p95 improving.

Jonathan L: For RCA notes: we should gather: full apt logs from all nodes, `dmesg` logs showing futex backtraces, perf perf.data from affected hosts, a subset of traces (span-level) showing where in the service stack calls are stuck. Also need to check any scheduler tunables that changed in the kernel patch.

Ben T: Collected spans: example trace (shortened):
```
span: request/serve
  child: model/infer (duration 60ms)
  child: kernel/futex_wait (duration 850ms)
  child: grpc/send (duration 10ms)
```
That `kernel/futex_wait` synthetic span is added by our tracer on host to highlight blocking syscall time.

Alice K: Customer comms: Leah, please send a follow-up noting mitigation completed and that we are investigating root cause. Keep SLA/status message updated.

Leah C: Sent update to impacted customers and posted incident notice in status.redwood.ai -> "Mitigation in progress, partial recovery observed after rollback of kernel on canary host; engineering investigating root cause."

Priya S: Added immediate observability action items: 1) new alert for host-level futex/syscall tail > 200ms, 2) perf-counter alert for softirq surge, 3) add node kernel version tagging to our latency dashboards so same correlation is easier next time.

Ben T: Next steps for full RCA: - Collect all kernel logs and perf data, - Reproduce locally if vendor provides kernel patch diff, - Narrow down which kernel subsystems (futex, sched, rt) cause the latency, - Work with cloud infra to block the kernel package in the repo until a patch.

Jonathan L: I'm opening a Jira: INFRA-1429 "Latency regression - suspected kernel 5.15.0-1024 futex scheduling regression". Assigning to eng-sre + infra. Include timeline and artifacts links.

Dave P: Postmortem owners: eng-sre to own technical RCA, eng-runtime to own service-level guidance (tracing + futex instrumentation), support to own customer follow-ups. Target: preliminary RCA in 48 hours.

Alice K: Closing loop: immediate incident mitigated (traffic rerouted, canary rollback), customer impact limited to increased latency/timeouts for a subset of customers, no data loss. Thanks everyone for quick action. I'll mark incident as "mitigated" in PD and hand off to the RCA owners. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident status changed to MITIGATED by Alice K. PagerDuty incident will be left open for RCA until INFRA-1429 is resolved.

(End of thread)
